subject.title: fix: reload Codex daemon after account promotion

question: Should this compatibility-sensitive account-promotion behavior be accepted only after redacted live proof demonstrates the managed daemon reload with two real accounts and preserved remote-control mode on the rebased head?
rationale: Injected command-runner tests cover the decision matrix, but only a real managed daemon can verify the installed Codex CLI lifecycle contract, active-auth handoff, and user-visible recovery behavior without risking a stale app-server identity.

options.title: Require rebased live proof
options.body: Require a redacted two-account managed-daemon run after resolving the dirty merge state, including the remote-control preservation and partial-failure recovery paths.

options.title: Accept test-only coverage
options.body: Merge based on the focused tests and documented upstream contract, accepting that real local daemon lifecycle behavior was not observed on the final head.

recommendation.title: Require rebased live proof
recommendation.body: Require a redacted two-account managed-daemon run after resolving the dirty merge state, including the remote-control preservation and partial-failure recovery paths.

likelyOwner.reason: The supplied branch history shows steipete authored the lifecycle rewrite and is the strongest available routing candidate for accepting its compatibility boundary.
